name: Afghanistan

flag.description: Three equal vertical bands of black, red and green, with the white national emblem (a mosque with a mihrab and minbar, framed by wheat sheaves and topped by the Shahada) centred over the red band.
flag.symbolism: Black is usually said to represent the troubled past, red the blood shed for independence, and green hope, prosperity and Islam.

hook: Afghanistan is a vertical black-red-green tricolour with a white mosque emblem on the red; Belgium is vertical black-yellow-red with no emblem.
trivia: Afghanistan changed its national flag more often during the 20th century than any other country.
The number 1298 under the mosque is the Solar Hijri year corresponding to 1919, when Afghanistan regained full independence.
Since 2021 the Taliban-led authorities in Kabul have used a white flag bearing the black Shahada; the tricolour shown here remains widely used abroad, including by the national cricket team.
